entry.title: Block-Reign: A Player vs AI Grid Game That Learns From You
entry.summary:
Most game AIs are fake smart.
Patterns, scripts, predictable behavior. Block-Reign isn’t. This is a lightweight Player vs AI grid battle game where the AI actually learns from every match you play — wins, losses, mistakes, all of it. No GPU.
No fancy engines.
Just Python, reinforcement learning, and persistence. Block-Reign is a 10×10 grid-based Player vs AI combat game built with: Flask + HTML for the frontend Python for the game server Reinforcement Learning (Q-Learning) for live gameplay DQN for advanced offline experimentation You play in the browser.
The AI plays on the server.
After every match, it gets smarter. The core idea was simple: What if the AI learned only from real games — not pre-trained data? So the AI: Starts dumb Learns only from actual matches
Saves its knowledge permanently Adapts to your playstyle
No synthetic data.
No scripted behaviors.
Just experience. The running server uses a Q-learning AI
After each completed match:
Match data is sent to the server The AI updates its Q-table Progress is saved on disk Restart the server → the AI remembers everything The project also includes a DQN trainer (ai_trainer.py) for experimentation. As of the latest run: Win rate: ~59% Matches played: 78 Record: 46 Wins / 36 Losses These stats are not hardcoded.
They are learned, stored, and persisted. Delete the training folder, and the AI forgets everything. 10×10 grid Arrow keys to move Space to shoot Simple mechanics, strategic positioning Fast matches, instant feedback Minimal visuals.
Maximum behavior learning. Delete: training/
or: training/models/simple_ai.pkl
Restart the server and play again.
The AI starts from scratch. This project wasn’t about graphics or polish. It was about: Understanding reinforcement learning Watching an AI evolve organically Building adaptive systems without massive compute https://github.com/DeveloperPuneet/Block-Reign Block-Reign isn’t perfect.
But it’s honest. An AI that earns its intelligence one loss at a time. And nah — this isn’t the end. comment
